title: Microsoft 365 Copilot connectors: people data with source-system access controls
summary: Hold: the deletion path omits the Copilot navigation step, and the assertion that every sensitive profile attribute is tenant-wide overlooks documented information barriers and profile access controls. The roadmap facts are accurate; the licensing field and connection-creation call also need small corrections.

claims.claim: Microsoft plans to import people data from external systems together with access control lists.
claims.quote: This release enables organizations to bring people data from external systems into Microsoft 365 along with associated access control lists (ACLs)

claims.claim: The planned capability makes Copilot respect source-system permissions.
claims.quote: ensuring Copilot respects existing permissions defined in source systems.

claims.claim: The planned imported data can be scoped to specific individuals and groups.
claims.quote: The imported data can be scoped to specific individuals and groups

claims.claim: Copilot is planned to reason over imported people data while honouring its access restrictions.
claims.quote: allowing Copilot to reason over people data while honoring access restrictions.

claims.where: summary; What's changing; controls[0].note; Risk assessment; rationale: risk
claims.claim: Today's documented default is that people connector data is visible to all tenant users.
claims.quote: By default, people data provided via a Copilot connector is visible to all users in the tenant.

claims.where: What's changing; Why it matters; controls[0].note; Risk assessment
claims.claim: Today's build guide requires granting everyone access in ingested items' ACLs.
claims.quote: You must set the access control list (ACL) on items ingested by the connector to grant access to everyone.

claims.where: What's changing; Risk assessment; Governance controls
claims.claim: Learn does not yet describe this roadmap feature or its differentiated people ACL mechanics.
claims.quote: Searched: people connectors differentiated access controls ACL individuals groups default rollout migration June 2027 561326; read graph/peopleconnectors and the people-data build guide, which still require everyone ACLs.

claims.where: What's changing; Cost and licensing; rationale: cost
claims.claim: Custom people connectors are built using Microsoft Graph external connections APIs.
claims.quote: You build Microsoft 365 Copilot connectors for people data in the same way that you build other Copilot connectors, by using the Microsoft Graph external connections APIs.

claims.claim: A people connection must set contentCategory to people.
claims.quote: Copilot connectors that contain people data must have the value `people` in the `contentCategory` property of the `externalConnections` API.

claims.claim: People connector data is stored in the user's Microsoft 365 profile.
claims.quote: This connector data is stored in the user's Microsoft 365 profile.

claims.claim: Uploaded people data is stored in the user's Exchange Online mailbox.
claims.quote: When you upload people data, each user's data attributes are scoped to their Microsoft 365 user profile and stored in the user's Exchange Online mailbox.

claims.where: front matter: defaultState; Why it matters
claims.claim: Microsoft has not stated the planned ACL control's default or whether existing connections change automatically.
claims.quote: Searched: people connectors differentiated access controls ACL individuals groups default rollout migration June 2027 561326; read the roadmap, graph/peopleconnectors and the people-data build guide; none states the new control's arrival default.

claims.where: Why it matters; Cost and licensing; Governance guidance; Open questions
claims.claim: No migration process for existing everyone-ACL people connections to differentiated ACLs is documented.
claims.quote: Searched: "people" "connectors" "ACL" "migration"; read graph/peopleconnectors, the people-data build guide and manage-access-permissions; only general delete-and-recreate guidance is stated.

claims.where: controls[1].note; Why it matters; Governance controls; Open questions
claims.claim: The general access-permissions page says updating permissions after creation is not currently supported.
claims.quote: Updating access permissions after you create the connection isn't currently supported.

claims.where: Why it matters; Governance guidance; Governance controls
claims.claim: Today's general connector guidance describes deleting and recreating a connection when its permission model is wrong.
claims.quote: In the connector pane, choose Delete to delete the existing connection. Recreate the connection using the Custom setup flow and explicitly configure access permissions.

claims.claim: Any sensitive attribute mapped into a profile is therefore tenant-wide.
claims.quote: Within your organization, this data is treated as organizational content and is subject to existing Microsoft 365 profile visibility and access controls. Microsoft 365 Copilot connectors for people data comply with information barriers (IB)
claims.fix: Replace 'Any sensitive attribute you map into a profile is therefore tenant-wide' with 'By default, people connector data is visible to all tenant users, subject to existing Microsoft 365 profile visibility and access controls and information barriers.' Keep the citation to https://learn.microsoft.com/graph/peopleconnectors.

claims.where: Risk assessment: Data exposure; rationale: impact
claims.claim: Connected people data can surface in Copilot and people search.
claims.quote: Adding people data to Microsoft Graph makes it available to Microsoft 365 Copilot and people experiences such as the profile card and people search.

claims.where: Risk assessment: Data exposure; Open questions
claims.claim: How planned differentiated ACLs apply to profile cards, Org Explorer and search is not documented.
claims.quote: Searched: people connectors differentiated access controls ACL individuals groups; "people connectors" "access" "Information barriers" "profile"; read graph/peopleconnectors and the build guide, which describe current profile controls, not future ACL reach.

claims.claim: People connectors respect Microsoft Purview Information Barriers.
claims.quote: Microsoft 365 Copilot connectors for people data comply with information barriers (IB) to ensure compliance across various platforms.

claims.claim: Microsoft does not describe the interaction between information barriers and the planned per-person ACLs.
claims.quote: Searched: "people connectors" "access" "Information barriers" "profile"; read graph/peopleconnectors and Learn information-barriers excerpts; they document existing barriers, not their interaction with planned differentiated ACLs.

claims.claim: Accounts that do not match a Microsoft Entra user are ignored.
claims.quote: Nonmatched user accounts (`userPrincipalName` or `externalDirectoryObjectId`) are ignored.

claims.claim: Microsoft Graph ignores accounts without an Exchange Online mailbox.
claims.quote: Microsoft Graph ignores accounts without an Exchange Online mailbox.

claims.claim: Mismatched identifiers silently drop data rather than produce a failure.
claims.quote: Searched: people data connectors nonmatched user accounts ignored silent errors diagnostics failure; read the people-data build guide and graph/peopleconnectors. They say accounts are ignored, but do not specify silence, diagnostics or failure responses.
claims.fix: Replace 'Mismatched identifiers in a source system would therefore silently drop data rather than fail' with 'Microsoft Graph ignores nonmatched user accounts.'

claims.claim: The cited sources describe ingestion and grounding, not a new write-action capability.
claims.quote: Searched: people connectors differentiated access controls ACL individuals groups; read the roadmap, graph/peopleconnectors and the people-data build guide; no new autonomous write-action capability is described.

claims.where: Risk assessment: Change & support; Governance guidance
claims.claim: People data connections do not support staged connections, so that route cannot be used for a pilot.
claims.quote: Connections with people data don't support staged connections.

claims.where: Risk assessment: Change & support; Governance guidance
claims.claim: Microsoft separately advises piloting people connectors with a limited audience.
claims.quote: Before rollout, confirm governance, privacy, and admin requirements for your connector and pilot with a limited audience.

claims.claim: Connector-ingested properties are read-only for users.
claims.quote: All properties ingested via the people connectors are read-only.

claims.claim: Microsoft recommends disabling user editing of properties also ingested through people connectors to avoid edits not appearing on profile cards.
claims.quote: We recommend that you disable user editing of any properties that are also ingested via people connectors to avoid scenarios where user edits aren't displayed on the profile card due to the precedence model.

claims.where: front matter: licensing.model; Cost and licensing
claims.claim: The licensing model is unknown because no licence specific to the new ACL option is published.
claims.quote: If your organization has Microsoft 365 Copilot licenses, connector grounding in Copilot is included, and no extra charges apply.
claims.fix: Set licensing.model to 'included'. Replace the first Cost and licensing paragraph with 'Connector grounding in Copilot is included with Microsoft 365 Copilot licences. Microsoft has not published a licence or price specific to the planned people-data ACL option.' Retain the general prerequisite details and citation to https://learn.microsoft.com/microsoft-365/copilot/connectors/prerequisites.

claims.where: licensing.notes; Cost and licensing; Scope; Open questions; rationale: cost
claims.claim: No licence or price specific to the planned people-data ACL capability is published, and the roadmap names none.
claims.quote: Searched: people data connectors licensing ACL pricing meter spending cap Microsoft 365 Copilot; read the roadmap, graph/peopleconnectors, the people-data build guide and connectors/prerequisites; no ACL-specific entitlement or price is stated.

claims.where: licensing.notes; Cost and licensing; rationale: cost

Microsoft 365 E7 | ✅ | ✅ | ✅

Microsoft 365 (any plan) | ✅ | ❌ | ❌

claims.claim: The general prerequisites page says indexing synced connector data incurs no extra cost for tenants with Microsoft 365 licences.
claims.quote: Indexing of synced connector data incurs no extra cost for tenants with Microsoft 365 licenses.

claims.claim: No meter, credit rate or spending cap specific to the planned ACL capability is documented.
claims.quote: Searched: people data connectors licensing ACL pricing meter spending cap Microsoft 365 Copilot; read connectors/prerequisites, graph/peopleconnectors and the build guide; results about Retrieval API billing do not state an ACL meter, rate or cap.

claims.claim: People data persists while its user is active and has a valid Microsoft 365 licence, subject to the deletion discussed elsewhere in the briefing.
claims.quote: People data is stored as long as the end user is active and has a valid Microsoft 365 license, provided no deletion request was made by the admin.

claims.quote: Searched: people connectors differentiated access controls ACL individuals groups default rollout migration June 2027 561326; read roadmap record, graph/peopleconnectors and the build guide; none states an ACL rollout channel or rollout procedure.

claims.where: controls[1].ui; Governance controls; Governance guidance: After rollout
claims.claim: The Permissions view is reached through Microsoft 365 admin center > Copilot > Connectors > Your Connections > select the connector > Permissions.
claims.quote: go to Copilot > Connectors > Your Connections. Select the connector you want to review to open the details pane. Under Permissions, you can view the permissions set for the connector.

claims.claim: No API equivalent for the connector-level Permissions view's source-ACL/everyone model is documented.
claims.quote: Searched: Microsoft Graph connectors view Permissions source ACL visible everyone API connection access permissions; read manage-access-permissions and externalConnection v1.0/beta properties; none exposes that connection-level model.

claims.claim: The Copilot Visibility toggle is reached through Microsoft 365 admin center > Copilot > Connectors > Your Connections > select the connection > Copilot Visibility.
claims.quote: Go to Copilot > Connectors > Your Connections. Select the connection that you want to modify. Under Copilot Visibility, select the toggle to turn the connector on or off

claims.claim: No documented API sets the same Copilot Search and Copilot Chat visibility toggle.
claims.quote: Searched: Microsoft Graph externalConnection Copilot Visibility enabledContentExperiences update connections; read manage-connector, externalConnection v1.0/beta, beta Update connection and connector experiences; no operation establishes this same toggle.

claims.claim: Learn describes Copilot Visibility for partner connectors, without explicitly confirming its use for people connectors.
claims.quote: Admins can control the visibility of partner connectors in Copilot and Copilot Search via a simple toggle.

claims.claim: Admin UI creation of custom people connectors is not documented.
claims.quote: Searched: custom people data connector create Microsoft 365 admin center UI; read graph/peopleconnectors and the build guide; returned UI setup for prebuilt BambooHR and custom federated connectors does not establish custom people-connector UI creation.

claims.claim: POST https://graph.microsoft.com/v1.0/external/connections creates a people connection with contentCategory set to people.
claims.quote:
POST https://graph.microsoft.com/v1.0/external/connections
In the request body, supply a JSON representation of the externalConnection object.
claims.fix: Set controls[3].api.call and its rendered table call to 'POST https://graph.microsoft.com/v1.0/external/connections'. Add to controls[3].note: 'The request body sets contentCategory to people.' Cite https://learn.microsoft.com/graph/api/resources/externalconnectors-externalconnection?view=graph-rest-1.0, whose property table permits people; the already-cited build guide requires it.

claims.claim: The deletion route starts at Microsoft 365 admin center > Connectors > Your Connections > select the connector > Delete.
claims.quote: In the Microsoft 365 Admin Center, go to Copilot > Connectors > Your Connections. Select the connector you want to review to open the details pane. In the connector pane, choose Delete to delete the existing connection.
claims.fix: Replace controls[4].ui.path and the rendered deletion path with 'Copilot > Connectors > Your Connections > select the connector > Delete'. Use https://learn.microsoft.com/microsoft-365/copilot/connectors/manage-access-permissions for ui.docs; retain https://learn.microsoft.com/graph/peopleconnectors as the source confirming deletion applies to people connectors.

claims.claim: DELETE https://graph.microsoft.com/v1.0/external/connections/{connectionId} deletes a connector connection.
Deleting a people connector removes it from all instances, with possible delays.
claims.quote: If a connector is deleted, it's removed from all instances, but delays can be expected.

claims.claim: Connectors can be inventoried at Copilot > Connectors > Your Connections, while the Graph management article uses Copilot > Agents and connectors.
claims.quote: A search admin can view and manage all the connections in the tenant via the Copilot > Agents and connectors section of the Microsoft 365 admin center.

claims.claim: Skills, positions, addresses and phones are examples of people attributes a connector can map.
claims.quote:

personAddresses | stringCollection | itemAddress
personPhones | stringCollection | itemPhone
personSkills | stringCollection | skillProficiency
